title: HfO2/SiO2 periodic Bragg stack with single defect cavity
scientific_hypothesis: A standard quarter-wave Bragg reflector pair (HfO2/SiO2) with a single half-wave defect cavity can achieve high transmission in 255-280 nm while blocking 300-1100 nm within 30 layers.
design_principle: Bragg reflectors create high reflectance outside the passband through constructive interference of reflections from periodic high/low index interfaces. A defect layer in the center creates a transmission resonance within the stopband.
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 15 layers (7 pairs + 1 cavity + 7 pairs)
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count is 15, well under 30-layer limit
HfO2 and SiO2 are conventional e-beam or ion-assisted depositable materials
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for Bragg reflectors
Defect mode theory for cavity resonance
Transfer matrix method for multilayer calculation
expected_advantages: HfO2/SiO2 pair has good UV transparency down to ~250 nm
known_risks: HfO2 may have increased absorption below 260 nm
Single cavity may not provide sharp enough passband edges
Blocking bandwidth may be insufficient for 300-1100 nm range
execution_request_english: Design a defect-cavity bandpass filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack: 7 periods of HfO2/SiO2 (Gao) quarter-wave pairs, one HfO2 cavity layer at center, then 7 periods of SiO2 (Gao)/HfO2 quarter-wave pairs. Total 15 layers. Optimize all individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm while minimizing transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Materials: hfo2, SiO2 (Gao).
